correctness.rationale: The cyclic Dirichlet spacing identity gives each consecutive block the exactly normalized Beta(j,N-j) law. Substitution of two finite beta-log expectations and an explicit harmonic-number interchange establishes the exact mean. The strict trapezoidal remainder yields positive and strictly decreasing increments of F_N, then strictly decreasing G_N=N(F_{N+1}-F_N)-F_N; rational interval checks certify the only four boundary signs needed for the global transition and unique maximum. The expansion follows from the same integral. The standalone standard-library checker reproduced all four rational signs, two independent finite-expectation formulas, and seeded Dirichlet simulations; simulations are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The statistic is a named, naturally normalized goodness-of-fit score for fully specified continuous nulls. Its defining paper uses approximate unit-mean null calibration. The exact nonlinear finite-sample mean, unique crossing at n=19/20, unique maximum at n=54 and asymptotic discrepancy characterize the entire natural sample-size parameter, replacing an approximation by an exact benchmark for moment-matched calibration and simulation validation. The gap is large for tiny samples, while its modest peak above one is stated without exaggeration; no power gain or exact critical-value claim is made.
